Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members. Brightline would separately pay up to $7 million in court-approved fees and expenses; any amount not awarded would go to the class. This structure delivers direct relief without requiring members to file claims.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments are appropriate given Brightline’s records. To move toward a settlement that provides direct relief and is supportable in court, we propose a $28 million class fund plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement on automatic payments and directing any unawarded fees to the class. To narrow the gap, we propose a $30 million class fund and up to $6 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses, with the other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement. We can increase the class fund to $29 million and maintain up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Automatic payments and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class remain important to a durable settlement.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. If Brightline can increase the class fund to $30 million, we can accept the $5 million cap on court-approved fees and expenses. Payments would remain automatic, and any fees not awarded would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We propose a $35 million class fund with automatic payments to all identified members, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any amount the court does not award in fees would go to the class. We are ready to discuss the figures, but an automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We agree that payments should be automatic. Your proposed $41 million total exceeds Brightline’s settlement authority. We propose a $29 million class fund plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. To bridge the gap, we can reduce our requested fees to $5 million if Brightline increases the class fund to $32 million. Fees would remain subject to court approval.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: Thank you for reducing the proposed fees. We can raise the class fund to $30 million, alongside up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with automatic payments and any unawarded fees going to the class.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We are close. We can meet halfway on the class fund at $31 million, with the same $5 million fee request subject to court approval, automatic payments, and any unawarded fees going to the class. Brightline would not be required to refrain from opposing the fee request.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic payments, since Brightline can identify and pay every affected member. Request a separately paid fee proportionate to the fund and litigation risk, with any fee reduction benefiting the class rather than reverting to Brightline.
Open with substantial automatic relief for the identifiable class. Keep fees separate and proportionate, and ensure any fee reduction benefits the class rather than reverting to Brightline.

Hargrove’s $39 million proposal is within authority, but there is room to negotiate a lower total. Whitcombe’s $41 million proposal exceeds authority. Automatic payments and fee savings flowing to the class support court approval.

Defense has accepted automatic distribution and class-benefiting treatment of unawarded fees. Its $28 million fund is a credible starting point, but there is room to negotiate improved class recovery and a fee request reflecting the work and risk, subject to court approval.

The defense offer provides automatic payments and sends any unawarded fees to the class, both important protections. Its $29 million class fund is credible given litigation and certification risks, but there is room to negotiate in round 2. A $32 million fund with the proposed $5 million fee preserves the protections while narrowing the total-price gap.

Both current offers are within authority, but there are four rounds remaining and room to improve the total cash outlay. Preserve automatic distribution and court-approval-friendly fee terms while making incremental counteroffers.

The $29 million automatic-payment fund is substantial, but there is time to seek a modest improvement for the class. Keep the fee at $5 million rather than making class relief contingent on a higher fee.

The $30 million automatic class fund is substantial, but there are three rounds left and the parties are only $2 million apart. A $31 million counteroffer preserves automatic payments and directs any unawarded fees to the class, while leaving a reasonable path to agreement.

Hargrove's $35 million total is within authority, cheaper than Whitcombe's $36 million proposal, and provides automatic distribution with court-reviewable fees. Accept Hargrove and do not enter a competing agreement.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: Hargrove Lane LLP and Brightline’s counsel reached the settlement through three rounds of negotiations. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were discussed together from the first round; fees were not deferred until after agreement on class relief. The resulting agreement provides a $30 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members without a claims process. Brightline will separately pay up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees the court does not award will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. The settlement remains subject to court approval.
